GenericAgent is an open-source Python framework that gives any LLM nine atomic tools, a five-layer on-demand memory, and a self-evolution loop that crystallizes each verified task trajectory into a reusable skill stored inL3. GenericAgent argues this is a density problem, not a length problem. The arXiv abstract says it directly: long-horizon performance is determined by how much decision-relevant information is maintained inside a finite context budget. The framework treats memory as the first-class object and tools as a thin interface over it, instead of the other way around. | Piece | One-line role | | --- | --- | | Agent Loop | ~100-line core inagent_loop.py that perceives, reasons, calls a tool, then writes results back to memory. | | Atomic Tools | Seven action tools plus two memory tools that act as the agent's only system interface. | | Layered Memory (L0–L4) | Hierarchical memory from meta rules through session archive, surfaced on demand instead of dumped into context. | | Skill Crystallization | Verified trajectories become reusable SOPs and executable code, written toL3 for later one-line invocation. | | Context Compression | Truncation and summarization layer that maintains information density across long executions. | is the smallest piece of the . It reads instruction, fetches L0 meta rules and the L1 insight index, decides which tool to call, executes, and writes results back. The README says it is roughly one hundred lines. The merged April 25 PR titled fix: ga global command cwd should follow user launch directory patches a bug here, where os join(script_dir, "temp") ignored the user's When a task succeeds and verifies, the agent rewrites the trajectory into either a structured SOP (procedure with parameters) or an executable script (Python that callscode_run`). That artefact is stored in L3 with an index entry in L1. Next time, L1 routes to L3 directly and the agent skips exploration. Open issue #386 (April 24, 2026) proposes an idle-time loop that consolidates redundant L3 entries, which is a sign the team takes skill-tree bloat seriously. Reddit hype. A late-April 2026 r/WebAfterAI thread listed GenericAgent in its top ten trending GitHub repos that “replace ~$1,000/month in paid AI tools,” pitching it as a direct replacement for paid agent infrastructure. r/AISEOInsider published a YouTube-linked thread titled “Generic Agent: FREE Self Evolving Autonomous AI Agent.” That kind of headline framing is hype, not analysis, but the discovery channel is real. GenericAgent is an open-source, ~3K-line Python agent framework from lsdefine that gives any LLM nine atomic tools, a five-layer memory, and a self-evolution loop that turns each solved task into a reusable skill. The skill tree is the L3 layer of memory. Each verified task trajectory is crystallized into a reusable SOP or executable script, written to disk, and recalled on the next similar request.
